q1: SELECT ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR GROUP BY ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(*)>=3
q2: SELECT DISTINCT ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR GROUP BY ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(TIMESTAMP) >= 3
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR GROUP BY ACTOR_ID,DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(*)>=3
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID FROM ACTORDIRECTOR GROUP BY ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID HAVING COUNT(TIMESTAMP) >= 3
counterexample: INSERT INTO ACTORDIRECTOR (TIMESTAMP, ACTOR_ID, DIRECTOR_ID) VALUES (1, 1, 1), (1, 1, 1), (2, 1, 1), (3, 1, 1);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 groups by ACTOR_ID and DIRECTOR_ID and checks if the count of rows is >= 3, while Q2 groups by ACTOR_ID and DIRECTOR_ID and checks if the count of TIMESTAMP values is >= 3. The count of rows and the count of TIMESTAMP values can be different if there are duplicate TIMESTAMP values in the ACTORDIRECTOR table.
counterexample_dsp: The difference is triggered when there are duplicate TIMESTAMP values in the ACTORDIRECTOR table.
